units.zh: 自周、陳以上，雅鄭淆雜而無別，隋文帝始分雅、俗二部，至唐更曰「部當」。
units.en: Through the Zhou and Chen era, court and popular music ran together without clear separation until Sui Wendi split them into elegant and popular bureaus; under Tang the categories were renamed "section assignments."
units.literal: From the Zhou and Chen [dynasties] upward, elegant and Zheng music were confused and mixed without distinction; Emperor Wen of Sui first divided them into elegant and popular two sections; in Tang they were further called "section assignments."

units.zh: 凡所謂俗樂者，二十有八調：正宮、高宮、中呂宮、道調宮、南呂宮、仙呂宮、黃鐘宮為七宮；
units.en: So-called popular music has twenty-eight modes: the seven palace modes are Zhenggong, Gaogong, Zhonglü Palace, Daodiao Palace, Nanlü Palace, Xianlü Palace, and Huangzhong Palace;
units.literal: What is called popular music comprises twenty-eight modes: Zhenggong, Gaogong, Zhonglü Palace, Daodiao Palace, Nanlü Palace, Xianlü Palace, and Huangzhong Palace are the seven palace modes;

units.zh: 越調、大食調、高大食調、雙調、小食調、歇指調、林鐘商為七商；
units.en: the seven shang modes are Yuediao, Dashidiao, Gaodashidiao, Shuangdiao, Xiaoshidiao, Xiezhidiao, and Linzhong Shang;
units.literal: Yuediao, Dashidiao, Gaodashidiao, Shuangdiao, Xiaoshidiao, Xiezhidiao, and Linzhong Shang are the seven shang modes;

units.zh: 大食角、高大食角，雙角，小食角、歇指角、林鐘角、越角為七角；
units.en: the seven jiao modes are Dashijiao, Gaodashijiao, Shuangjiao, Xiaoshijiao, Xiezhijiao, Linzhong Jiao, and Yuejiao;
units.literal: Dashijiao, Gaodashijiao, Shuangjiao, Xiaoshijiao, Xiezhijiao, Linzhong Jiao, and Yuejiao are the seven jiao modes;

units.zh: 中呂調、正平調、高平調、仙呂調，黃鐘羽。
units.en: and the yu modes are Zhonglü Diao, Zhengping Diao, Gaoping Diao, Xianlü Diao, and Huangzhong Yu.
units.literal: Zhonglü Diao, Zhengping Diao, Gaoping Diao, Xianlü Diao, and Huangzhong Yu.

units.zh: 般涉調、高般涉為七羽。
units.en: Banshe Diao and Gaobanshe complete the seven yu modes.
units.literal: Banshe Diao and Gaobanshe are the seven yu modes.

units.zh: 皆從濁至清，迭更其聲，下則益濁，上則益清，慢者過節，急者流蕩。
units.en: Pitch moves from low and thick to high and bright by degrees; lower lines grow heavier, higher lines thinner; slow tempi drag past the beat, quick ones spill over.
units.literal: All proceed from muddy to clear, changing their sound in turn; going down grows muddier, going up grows clearer; slow passages overshoot the beat, fast ones run wild.

units.zh: 其後聲器浸殊，或有宮調之名，或以倍四為度，有與律呂同名，而聲不近雅者。
units.en: Later instruments and tones diverged: some pieces kept palace-mode labels, some took the doubled-fourth interval as their frame, and some borrowed pitch-pipe names while sounding far from court style.
units.literal: Later the timbres gradually diverged; some bore palace-mode names, some used doubled-fourth as their measure; some shared names with the pitch pipes yet sounded nothing like elegant music.

units.zh: 其宮調乃應夾鐘之律，燕設用之。
units.en: The palace mode in question matched the Jiazhong pipe and was reserved for feast settings.
units.literal: That palace mode answered to the Jiazhong pitch pipe and was used at banquets.

units.zh: 絲有琵琶、五弦、箜篌、箏，竹有觱篥、簫、笛，匏有笙，革有杖鼓、第二鼓、第三鼓、腰鼓、大鼓，土則附革而為鞡，木有拍板、方響，以體金應石而備八音。
units.en: Stringed instruments included pipa, five-string, konghou, and zheng; bamboo, bili, xiao, and flute; gourd, sheng; hide, staff, second, third, waist, and great drums; earth joined hide for the ta; wood, clappers and fangxiang—thus metal and stone, silk and bamboo, gourd and hide together filled the eight-tone set.
units.literal: Silk had pipa, five-string, konghou, and zheng; bamboo had bili, xiao, and di; gourd had sheng; hide had staff drum, second drum, third drum, waist drum, and great drum; earth was attached to hide to make the ta; wood had clappers and fangxiang—embodying metal and answering stone to complete the eight sounds.

units.zh: 倍四本屬清樂，形類雅音，而曲出於胡部。
units.en: The doubled-fourth scale came from clear music and looked like court style, but its tunes issued from the foreign repertoire.
units.literal: Doubled-fourth originally belonged to clear music; in form it resembled elegant sound, yet its pieces came from the barbarian bureau.

units.zh: 復有銀字之名，中管之格，皆前代應律之器也。
units.en: Terms like "silver character" and the middle-pipe register likewise denoted older pipe-tuned instruments.
units.literal: There were also names such as "silver character" and the middle-pipe register—all instruments of former ages that answered to the pitch pipes.

units.zh: 後人失其傳，而更以異名，故俗部諸曲，悉源于雅樂。
units.en: Later generations lost the tradition and renamed things, so every popular-bureau tune still traces back to elegant music at root.
units.literal: Later men lost the transmission and substituted other names; thus all pieces of the popular bureau ultimately stem from elegant music.

units.zh: 周、隋管弦雜曲數百，皆西涼樂也。
units.en: Zhou and Sui preserved hundreds of mixed orchestral pieces, all of Western Liang origin.
units.literal: The hundreds of mixed orchestral pieces of Zhou and Sui were all Western Liang music.

units.zh: 鼓舞曲，皆龜茲樂也。
units.en: Dance pieces with drum accompaniment were Kucha in origin.
units.literal: Drum-and-dance pieces were all Kucha music.

units.zh: 唯琴工猶傳楚、漢舊聲及《清調》，蔡邕五弄、楚調四弄，謂之九弄。
units.en: Only qin masters still carried Chu and Han legacy tunes and the Clear Mode—Cai Yong's five suites plus the Chu mode's four, known together as the Nine Suites.
units.literal: Only qin players still transmitted old Chu and Han sounds and the "Clear Mode"; Cai Yong's five suites and the Chu mode's four suites were called the nine suites.

units.zh: 隋亡，清樂散缺，存者才六十三曲。
units.en: After Sui's collapse clear music broke apart; barely sixty-three pieces remained.
units.literal: When Sui fell, clear music scattered and was lost; only sixty-three pieces survived.

units.zh: 其後傳者：《平調》、《清調》，周《房中樂》遺聲也；
units.en: Pieces still handed down included Plain Mode and Clear Mode, Zhou survivals from inner-chamber music;
units.literal: Those transmitted later: "Plain Mode" and "Clear Mode" are survivals of Zhou inner-chamber music;

units.zh: 《白雪》，楚曲也；
units.en: "White Snow," a Chu melody;
units.literal: "White Snow" is a Chu tune;

units.zh: 《公莫舞》，漢舞也；
units.en: "Lord, do not!" a Han dance piece;
units.literal: "Lord, do not!" is a Han dance;

units.zh: 《巴渝》，漢高帝命工人作也；
units.en: "Bayu," commissioned by Han Gaozu from his artisans;
units.literal: "Bayu" was made when Emperor Gaozu of Han ordered craftsmen to compose it;

units.zh: 《明君》，漢元帝時作也；
units.en: "Bright Lady," from Han Yuandi's reign;
units.literal: "Bright Lady" was composed in the time of Emperor Yuan of Han;

units.zh: 《明之君》，漢《鞞舞》曲也；
units.en: "Bright Lord," a Han shield-dance tune;
units.literal: "Bright Lord" is a Han "Shield Dance" tune;

units.zh: 《鐸舞》，漢曲也；
units.en: "Duo Dance," Han in origin;
units.literal: "Duo Dance" is a Han tune;

units.zh: 《白鳩》，吳《拂舞》曲也；
units.en: "White Dove," from Wu's whisk dance;
units.literal: "White Dove" is a Wu "Whisk Dance" tune;

units.zh: 《白紵》，吳舞也；
units.en: "White Ramie," a Wu dance;
units.literal: "White Ramie" is a Wu dance;

units.zh: 《子夜》，晉曲也；
units.en: "Midnight," Jin;
units.literal: "Midnight" is a Jin tune;

units.zh: 《前溪》，晉車騎將軍沈珫作也；
units.en: "Front Brook," by Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Chong;
units.literal: "Front Brook" was composed by Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Chong;

units.zh: 《團扇》，晉王瑉歌也；
units.en: "Round Fan," a song by Jin Wang Min;
units.literal: "Round Fan" is a song by Jin Wang Min;

units.zh: 《懊儂》，晉隆安初謠也；
units.en: "Regretful Lover," a ballad from early Jin Long'an;
units.literal: "Regretful Lover" is a ballad from early Long'an of Jin;

units.zh: 《長史變》，晉司徒左長史王廞作也；
units.en: "Chief Clerk Variation," by Jin Left Chief Clerk Wang Xin;
units.literal: "Chief Clerk Variation" was composed by Jin Left Chief Clerk of the Minister Wang Xin;

units.zh: 《丁督護》，晉、宋間曲也；
units.en: "Ding, the Chief Steward," from the Jin–Song interval;
units.literal: "Ding, the Chief Steward" is a tune from between Jin and Song;

units.zh: 《讀曲》，宋人為彭城王義康作也；
units.en: "Reading Tune," composed in Song for Prince of Pengcheng Yikang;
units.literal: "Reading Tune" was made by a Song man for Prince of Pengcheng Yikang;

units.zh: 《烏夜啼》，宋臨川王義慶作也；
units.en: "Crow Cries at Night," by Song Prince of Linchuan Yiqing;
units.literal: "Crow Cries at Night" was composed by Song Prince of Linchuan Yiqing;

units.zh: 《石城》，宋臧質作也；
units.en: "Stone City," by Song Zang Zhi;
units.literal: "Stone City" was composed by Song Zang Zhi;

units.zh: 《莫愁》《石城樂》所出也；
units.en: "Mochou" grew out of "Stone City Music";
units.literal: "Mochou" derives from "Stone City Music";

units.zh: 《襄陽》，宋隨王誕作也；
units.en: "Xiangyang," by Song Prince of Sui Dan;
units.literal: "Xiangyang" was composed by Song Prince of Sui Wang Dan;

units.zh: 《烏夜飛》，宋沈攸之作也；
units.en: "Crow Flies at Night," by Song Shen Youzhi;
units.literal: "Crow Flies at Night" was composed by Song Shen Youzhi;

units.zh: 《估客樂》，齊武帝作也；
units.en: "Merchant's Song," by Qi Emperor Wu;
units.literal: "Merchant's Song" was composed by Qi Emperor Wu;

units.zh: 《楊叛》，北齊歌也；
units.en: "Yang the Rebel," a Northern Qi song;
units.literal: "Yang the Rebel" is a Northern Qi song;

units.zh: 《驍壺》，投壺樂也；
units.en: "Valiant Pot," music for pitch-pot play;
units.literal: "Valiant Pot" is pitch-pot music;

units.zh: 《常林歡》，宋、梁間曲也；
units.en: "Changlin Joy," from the Song–Liang period;
units.literal: "Changlin Joy" is a tune from between Song and Liang;

units.zh: 《三洲》，商人歌也；
units.en: "Three Isles," a merchants' song;
units.literal: "Three Isles" is a merchant's song;

units.zh: 《採桑》，《三洲曲》所出也；
units.en: "Picking Mulberry," spun from the Three Isles tune;
units.literal: "Picking Mulberry" derives from the "Three Isles Tune";

units.zh: 《玉樹後庭花》、《堂堂》，陳後主作也；
units.en: "Jade Tree in the Rear Court" and "Stately," by Chen's last emperor;
units.literal: "Jade Tree in the Rear Court" and "Stately" were composed by Chen Last Lord;

units.zh: 《泛龍舟》，隋煬帝作也。
units.en: "Floating Dragon Boat," by Sui Yangdi.
units.literal: "Floating Dragon Boat" was composed by Emperor Yang of Sui.

units.zh: 又有《吳聲四時歌》、《雅歌》、《上林》、《鳳雛》、《平折》、《命嘯》等曲，其聲與其辭皆訛失，十不傳其一二。
units.en: Other titles—"Wu Sound Four Seasons Song," "Elegant Song," "Upper Grove," "Phoenix Chick," "Level Bend," "Commanding Cry"—survived only in name; music and text alike are garbled, and scarcely one piece in ten still passes down intact.
units.literal: There were also tunes such as "Wu Sound Four Seasons Song," "Elegant Song," "Upper Grove," "Phoenix Chick," "Level Bend," and "Commanding Cry"; both their sounds and their texts are corrupted and lost—not one or two in ten are transmitted.

units.zh: 蓋唐自太宗、高宗作三大舞，雜用於燕樂，其他諸曲出於一時之作，雖非純雅，尚不至於淫放。
units.en: Broadly speaking, Taizong and Gaozong gave Tang three great dances used in banquet music; other pieces were occasional works—not wholly refined, but not yet dissolute.
units.literal: Broadly, from Taizong and Gaozong Tang composed three great dances, mingling them in banquet music; other tunes arose from momentary composition—though not purely elegant, they had not yet sunk to licentious excess.

units.zh: 武后之禍，繼以中宗昏亂，固無足言者。
units.en: The catastrophe of Empress Wu and Zhongzong's benighted reign scarcely need be discussed.
units.literal: The disaster of Empress Wu, followed by Zhongzong's benighted disorder, scarcely warrants mention.

units.zh: 玄宗為平王，有散樂一部，定韋后之難，頗有預謀者。
units.en: As Prince of Ping, Xuanzong maintained a miscellany-music troupe and had taken no small part in planning the overthrow of Empress Wei.
units.literal: When Xuanzong was Prince of Ping he kept a bureau of miscellany music; in settling the crisis of Empress Wei he had shared much in the plotting.

units.zh: 及即位，命寧王主藩邸樂，以亢太常，分兩朋以角優劣。
units.en: Once enthroned he put the Prince of Ning in charge of mansion music to rival the Grand Music Office, pitting two parties against each other in contest.
units.literal: On his accession he charged the Prince of Ning with music at the princely mansion to rival Grand Music, dividing two factions to compete for superiority.

units.zh: 置內教坊於蓬萊宮側，居新聲、散樂、倡優之伎，有諧謔而賜金帛朱紫者，酸棗縣尉袁楚客上疏極諫。
units.en: He set up an Inner Music Office beside Penglai Palace for new songs, miscellany pieces, and performers; when jesters were rewarded with gold, silk, and purple robes, Yuan Chuke, lieutenant of Suanzao county, submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance.
units.literal: He established the Inner Music Office beside Penglai Palace to house new tunes, miscellany music, and entertainer skills; when comic banter won gifts of gold, silk, and purple rank, Yuan Chuke, county lieutenant of Suanzao, submitted a memorial vehemently remonstrating.

units.zh: 初，帝賜第隆慶坊，坊南之地變為池，中宗常泛舟以厭其祥。
units.en: Early on the emperor received a residence in Longqing Ward; the ground south of it became a pond, and Zhongzong would row there to dispel the ill omen.
units.literal: At first the emperor was granted a mansion in Longqing Ward; the land south of the ward turned into a pool, and Zhongzong often went boating to suppress the omen.

units.zh: 帝即位，作《龍池樂》，舞者十有二人，冠芙蓉冠，躡履，備用雅樂，唯無磬。
units.en: On his accession he created "Dragon Pool Music," danced by twelve performers in lotus crowns and soft shoes to court instrumentation—everything but the stone chimes.
units.literal: When the emperor took the throne he composed "Dragon Pool Music": twelve dancers wearing lotus crowns and treading shoes, furnished with elegant music save for no stone chimes.

units.zh: 又作《聖壽樂》，以女子衣五色繡襟而舞之。
units.en: He also wrote "Holy Longevity Music," performed by women in five-colored embroidered collars.
units.literal: He also composed "Holy Longevity Music," danced by women in five-colored embroidered collars.

units.zh: 又作《小破陣樂》，舞者被甲胄。
units.en: He added "Little Breaking the Formation," its dancers in armor.
units.literal: He also composed "Little Breaking the Formation Music"; the dancers wore armor.

units.zh: 又作《光聖樂》，舞者烏冠、畫衣，以歌王跡所興。
units.en: He also made "Radiant Sage Music," with dancers in black caps and painted robes praising the royal path he had opened.
units.literal: He also composed "Radiant Sage Music"; dancers wore black caps and painted robes to sing of the kingly trace he had raised.

units.zh: 又分樂為二部：堂下立奏，謂之立部伎；
units.en: Music was then split into two troupes: pieces played standing in the hall court were the Standing Bureau;
units.literal: He further divided music into two bureaus: performance standing below the hall was called the Standing Bureau;

units.zh: 堂上坐奏，謂之坐部伎。
units.en: those played seated on the dais were the Seated Bureau.
units.literal: performance seated in the hall was called the Seated Bureau.

units.zh: 太常閱坐部，不可教者隸立部，又不可教者，乃習雅樂。
units.en: The Court of Sacrifices auditioned the Seated Bureau; performers who could not be trained there dropped to the Standing Bureau, and if still hopeless they were sent to elegant music.
units.literal: The Director of Court Music reviewed the Seated Bureau; those unteachable were assigned to the Standing Bureau, and if still unteachable they studied elegant music.

units.zh: 立部伎八：一《安舞》，二《太平樂》，三《破陣樂》，四《慶善樂》，五《大定樂》，六《上元樂》，七《聖壽樂》，八《光聖樂》。
units.en: The Standing Bureau numbered eight works: Peace Dance, Great Peace Music, Breaking the Formation, Celebrating Goodness, Great Settlement, Upper Prime, Holy Longevity, and Radiant Sage.
units.literal: Eight pieces of the Standing Bureau: first "Peace Dance," second "Great Peace Music," third "Breaking the Formation Music," fourth "Celebrating Goodness Music," fifth "Great Settlement Music," sixth "Upper Prime Music," seventh "Holy Longevity Music," eighth "Radiant Sage Music."

units.zh: 《安舞》、《太平樂》，周、隋遺音也。
units.en: "Peace Dance" and "Great Peace Music" preserve Zhou and Sui legacy.
units.literal: "Peace Dance" and "Great Peace Music" are survivals of Zhou and Sui sound.

units.zh: 《破陣樂》以下皆用大鼓，雜以龜茲樂，其聲震厲。
units.en: From Breaking the Formation onward every piece used great drums with Kucha music—sound sharp enough to startle.
units.literal: From "Breaking the Formation Music" downward all used great drums mixed with Kucha music; the sound was thunderous and fierce.

units.zh: 《大定樂》又加金鉦。
units.en: "Great Settlement Music" layered in golden cymbals.
units.literal: "Great Settlement Music" added golden cymbals as well.

units.zh: 《慶善舞》顓用西涼樂，聲頗閒雅。
units.en: "Celebrating Goodness Dance" relied wholly on Western Liang music and sounded notably calm and elegant.
units.literal: "Celebrating Goodness Dance" exclusively used Western Liang music; the sound was quite leisurely and refined.

units.zh: 每享郊廟，則《破陣》、《上元》、《慶善》三舞皆用之。
units.en: At every suburban and temple sacrifice the three dances Breaking the Formation, Upper Prime, and Celebrating Goodness were performed.
units.literal: Whenever suburban and ancestral temples were feasted, the three dances "Breaking the Formation," "Upper Prime," and "Celebrating Goodness" were all used.

units.zh: 坐部伎六：一《燕樂》，二《長壽樂》，三《天授樂》，四《鳥歌萬歲樂》，五《龍池樂》，六《小破陣樂》。
units.en: The Seated Bureau had six: Banquet Music, Longevity Music, Heaven-Bestowed Music, Bird Song of Ten Thousand Years, Dragon Pool, and Little Breaking the Formation.
units.literal: Six pieces of the Seated Bureau: first "Banquet Music," second "Longevity Music," third "Heaven-Bestowed Music," fourth "Bird Song of Ten Thousand Years Music," fifth "Dragon Pool Music," sixth "Little Breaking the Formation Music."

units.zh: 《天授》、《鳥歌》，皆武后作也。
units.en: Heaven-Bestowed and Bird Song both came from Empress Wu.
units.literal: "Heaven-Bestowed" and "Bird Song" were both composed by Empress Wu.

units.zh: 天授，年名。
units.en: Heaven-Bestowed was her reign era name.
units.literal: Heaven-Bestowed is a reign title.

units.zh: 鳥歌者，有鳥能人言萬歲，因以制樂。
units.en: Bird Song arose when a bird was said to cry "ten thousand years," inspiring the piece.
units.literal: As for Bird Song: a bird could speak "ten thousand years," and music was composed on that account.

units.zh: 自《長壽樂》以下，用龜茲舞，唯《龍池樂》則否。
units.en: From Longevity Music down the Kucha dance style was used—Dragon Pool alone excepted.
units.literal: From "Longevity Music" downward Kucha dance was used; only "Dragon Pool Music" did not.

units.zh: 是時，民間以帝自潞州還京師，舉兵夜半誅韋皇后，制《夜半樂》、《還京樂》二曲。
units.en: Popular musicians then wrote "Midnight Music" and "Returning to the Capital," commemorating his midnight march from Luzhou to kill Empress Wei.
units.literal: At that time the people, because the emperor had returned from Luzhou to the capital at midnight and raised troops to execute Empress Wei, composed the two tunes "Midnight Music" and "Returning to the Capital Music."

units.zh: 帝又作《文成曲》，與《小破陣樂》更奏之。
units.en: He also wrote "Wencheng Tune," paired in rotation with Little Breaking the Formation.
units.literal: The emperor also composed "Wencheng Tune" and alternated it with "Little Breaking the Formation Music."

units.zh: 其後，河西節度使楊敬忠獻《霓裳羽衣曲》十二遍，凡曲終必遽，唯《霓裳羽衣曲》將畢，引聲益緩。
units.en: Later Yang Jingzhong of Hexi presented the Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Robe in twelve passes; most suites rushed their endings, but this one deliberately slowed as it finished.
units.literal: Later Hexi Military Commissioner Yang Jingzhong presented the "Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Robe" in twelve repetitions; whenever a piece ended it always hurried, but as the "Rainbow Skirt" neared its close the leading sound grew ever slower.

units.zh: 帝方浸喜神仙之事，詔道士司馬承禎制《玄真道曲》，茅山道士李會元制《大羅天曲》，工部侍郎賀知章制《紫清上聖道曲》。
units.en: As his taste turned toward immortals he commissioned Sima Chengzhen's "Mysterious Truth Dao Tune," Li Huiyuan of Maoshan's "Great Luo Heaven Tune," and He Zhizhang's "Purple Clarity Supreme Sage Dao Tune."
units.literal: The emperor was then increasingly fond of immortal matters; he ordered Daoist priest Sima Chengzhen to compose "Mysterious Truth Dao Tune," Maoshan priest Li Huiyuan to compose "Great Luo Heaven Tune," and Ministry Vice Minister He Zhizhang to compose "Purple Clarity Supreme Sage Dao Tune."

units.zh: 太清宮成，太常卿韋縚制《景雲》、《九真》、《紫極》、《小長壽》、《承天》、《順天樂》六曲，又制商調《君臣相遇樂》曲。
units.en: At the Supreme Clarity Palace's completion Wei Tao, Director of Court Music, offered six pieces—Jingyun, Nine Perfections, Purple Pole, Little Longevity, Receiving Heaven, Following Heaven—and a shang-mode suite, Ruler and Minister Meeting in Joy.
units.literal: When the Supreme Clarity Palace was completed, Court Director Wei Tao composed six tunes—"Jingyun," "Nine Perfections," "Purple Pole," "Little Longevity," "Receiving Heaven," and "Following Heaven Music"—and also composed the shang-mode tune "Ruler and Minister Meeting in Joy."

units.zh: 初，隋有法曲，其音清而近雅。
units.en: Sui had long kept the fa tune, clear-toned and close to court style.
units.literal: At first Sui had the fa tune; its sound was clear and near to elegant.

units.zh: 其器有鐃、鈸、鐘、磬、幢簫、琵琶。
units.en: It used nao and bo cymbals, bells, stone chimes, banner flutes, and pipa.
units.literal: Its instruments were nao, bo, bell, stone chime, banner flute, and pipa.

units.zh: 琵琶圓體修頸而小，號曰「秦漢子」，蓋弦鞀之遺制，出於胡中，傳為秦、漢所作。
units.en: The pipa is round-bodied with a long thin neck—nicknamed "Qin-Han Son," a descendant of the string drum from the frontier, credited by tradition to Qin and Han times.
units.literal: The pipa has a round body, slender neck, and small size; it is called the "Qin-Han Son," being a legacy form of the string drum, coming from among the barbarians and handed down as the work of Qin and Han.

units.zh: 其聲金、石、絲、竹以次作，隋煬帝厭其聲澹，曲終復加解音。
units.en: Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo entered in turn; Sui Yangdi found the tone too plain and had ornamental figures added after every closing.
units.literal: Its sounds of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo were performed in sequence; Emperor Yang of Sui disliked its thin sound and after each piece added embellishing tones.

units.zh: 玄宗既知音律，又酷愛法曲，選坐部伎子弟三百教於梨園，聲有誤者，帝必覺而正之，號「皇帝梨園弟子」。
units.en: Xuanzong, himself versed in pitch, adored the fa tune and drilled three hundred Seated Bureau youths in the Pear Garden; he caught every wrong note and fixed it himself—hence "the emperor's Pear Garden disciples."
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong understood pitch law and dearly loved the fa tune; he chose three hundred Seated Bureau youths to teach in the Pear Garden, and if a note was wrong the emperor always noticed and corrected it—they were called "the emperor's Pear Garden disciples."

units.zh: 宮女數百，亦為梨園弟子，居宜春北院。
units.en: Hundreds of palace women joined as Pear Garden disciples in Yichun's north courtyard.
units.literal: Several hundred palace women also became Pear Garden disciples and lived in the north courtyard of Yichun.

units.zh: 梨園法部，更置小部音聲三十餘人。
units.en: Inside the Pear Garden's fa section he added a junior troupe of some thirty players.
units.literal: Within the Pear Garden fa section he further set up a small bureau of more than thirty musicians.

units.zh: 帝幸驪山，楊貴妃生日，命小部張樂長生殿，因奏新曲，未有名，會南方進荔枝，因名曰《荔枝香》。
units.en: At Mount Li on Yang Guifei's birthday the small bureau performed a new, unnamed work in the Hall of Long Life; southern lychees arrived that day, so the piece became "Lychee Fragrance."
units.literal: When the emperor visited Mount Li on Yang Guifei's birthday he ordered the small bureau to spread music in the Hall of Long Life; as they played a new piece still without a name, lychees arrived from the south, and it was therefore named "Lychee Fragrance."

units.zh: 帝又好羯鼓，而甯王善吹橫笛，達官大臣慕之，皆喜言音律。
units.en: He favored the jie drum while Prince of Ning led on transverse flute; courtiers copied them and music talk became fashion.
units.literal: The emperor also loved the jie drum, while Prince of Ning excelled at the transverse flute; high officials imitated them and all delighted in discussing pitch law.

units.zh: 帝嘗稱：「羯鼓，八音之領袖，諸樂不可方也。」
units.en: He once said, "The jie drum heads the eight tones—nothing else stands beside it."
units.literal: The emperor once declared: "The jie drum is the leader of the eight sounds; no other music can compare with it."

units.zh: 蓋本戎羯之樂，其音太蔟一均，龜茲、高昌、疏勒、天竺部皆用之，其聲焦殺，特異眾樂。
units.en: Rooted in frontier Jie drums, it sits in the Taicu register; Kucha, Gaochang, Shule, and Tianzhu pieces all draw on it—tone biting and dry, unlike anything else in the ensemble.
units.literal: It basically stems from Rong and Jie music; its pitch is the Taicu register; Kucha, Gaochang, Shule, and the Tianzhu bureau all use it; its sound is sharp and dry, utterly unlike other music.

units.zh: 開元二十四年，升胡部於堂上。
units.en: Kaiyuan 24 raised the foreign bureau to hall performance.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan the barbarian bureau was elevated to the hall.

units.zh: 而天寶樂曲，皆以邊地名，若《涼州》、《伊州》、《甘州》之類。
units.en: By the Tianbao reign most new tunes bore border place-names—Liangzhou, Yizhou, Ganzhou, and the like.
units.literal: Yet Tianbao era pieces mostly took frontier place-names, such as "Liangzhou," "Yizhou," and "Ganzhou."

units.zh: 後又詔道調、法曲與胡部新聲合作。
units.en: An edict then fused Daodiao, fa music, and fresh barbarian melodies.
units.literal: Later an edict ordered Daodiao, fa tunes, and new barbarian sounds to be combined.

units.zh: 明年，安祿山反，涼州、伊州、甘州皆陷吐蕃。
units.en: The following year An Lushan rose; Liangzhou, Yizhou, and Ganzhou were lost to Tibet.
units.literal: The next year An Lushan rebelled; Liangzhou, Yizhou, and Ganzhou all fell to Tibet.

units.zh: 唐之盛時，凡樂人、音聲人、太常雜戶子弟隸太常及鼓吹署，皆番上，總號音聲人，至數萬人。
units.en: At Tang's zenith every player, vocalist, and Court of Sacrifices or Drum-and-Pipe dependent rotated through service—tens of thousands in all, lumped together as "sound specialists."
units.literal: At Tang's height, all musicians, sound specialists, and sons of miscellaneous households attached to the Court of Sacrifices and the Drum-and-Pipe Office reported for duty in rotation; collectively they were called sound specialists, numbering up to tens of thousands.

units.zh: 玄宗又嘗以馬百匹，盛飾分左右，施三重榻，舞《傾杯》數十曲，壯士舉榻，馬不動。
units.en: He once arrayed a hundred richly caparisoned horses with triple couches and danced dozens of Tipping the Cup numbers while brawny men heaved the couches without budging the animals.
units.literal: Xuanzong also once took a hundred horses lavishly caparisoned left and right, set triple couches, and danced dozens of "Tipping the Cup" pieces; strong men lifted the couches yet the horses did not stir.

units.zh: 樂工少年姿秀者十數人，衣黃衫、文玉帶，立左右。
units.en: A dozen-odd handsome young players in yellow jackets and patterned jade belts flanked the scene.
units.literal: More than a dozen youthful, handsome musicians wore yellow jackets and patterned jade belts and stood left and right.

units.zh: 每千秋節，舞於勤政樓下，後賜宴設酺，亦會勤政樓。
units.en: Each Thousand Autumns Festival they danced beneath the Diligence-in-Government Tower; later court feasts with public wine met there too.
units.literal: Every Thousand Autumns Festival they danced below the Diligence-in-Government Tower; later banquets with communal wine also gathered at that tower.

units.zh: 其日未明，金吾引駕騎，北衙四軍陳仗，列旗幟，被金甲、短後繡袍。
units.en: Before dawn the Golden Crow guard led the cavalcade; four northern-yard armies formed ranks in golden armor and short embroidered surcoats.
units.literal: Before dawn that day the Golden Crow guard led the imperial escort; the four northern-yard armies deployed arms, lined banners and flags, wore golden armor and short embroidered rear-guards.

units.zh: 太常卿引雅樂，每部數十人，間以胡夷之技。
units.en: The Court Director led elegant music—dozens per section—punctuated by foreign acts.
units.literal: The Court Director led elegant music, several dozen per section, interspersed with barbarian skills.

units.zh: 內閑廄使引戲馬，五坊使引象、犀，入場拜舞。
units.en: The Inner Stud led performing horses; the Five Paddocks led elephants and rhinos to enter and bow in dance.
units.literal: The Inner Stud envoy led trick horses; the Five Paddocks envoy led elephants and rhinoceroses to enter the ground and bow in dance.

units.zh: 宮人數百衣錦繡衣，出帷中，擊雷鼓，奏《小破陣樂》，歲以為常。
units.en: Hundreds of palace women in brocade slipped from behind curtains, beat thunder drums, and played Little Breaking the Formation—an annual ritual.
units.literal: Several hundred palace women in brocade robes emerged from within the curtain, struck thunder drums, and performed "Little Breaking the Formation Music"—year after year as custom.

units.zh: 千秋節者，玄宗以八月五日生，因以其日名節，而君臣共為荒樂，當時流俗多傳其事以為盛。
units.en: The Thousand Autumns Festival marked Xuanzong's birthday on the eighth month's fifth day; court and emperor abandoned themselves to revelry, and contemporaries trumpeted the spectacle.
units.literal: The Thousand Autumns Festival: Xuanzong was born on the fifth day of the eighth month, and therefore named the festival for that day; ruler and ministers together indulged in reckless music, and popular custom widely transmitted the affair as splendor.

units.zh: 其後巨盜起，陷兩京，自此天下用兵不息，而離宮苑囿遂以荒堙，獨其餘聲遺曲傳人間，聞者為之悲涼感動。
units.en: Then rebellion took both capitals; war never lifted, pleasure parks rotted away, and only fragments of music wandered among common folk, stirring grief in whoever heard them.
units.literal: Later a great bandit arose and seized the two capitals; from then on warfare in the realm never ceased, while detached palaces and parks fell to ruin—only stray sounds and surviving tunes passed among the people, and hearers were moved to sorrow and chill.

units.zh: 蓋其事適足為戒，而不足考法，故不復著其詳。
units.en: The episode warns more than it instructs, so the account stops short of full detail.
units.literal: Those affairs are just enough to serve as warning and not enough to take as model; therefore the details are not recorded further.

units.zh: 自肅宗以後，皆以生日為節，而德宗不立節，然止於群臣稱觴上壽而已。
units.en: After Suzong emperors marked birthdays as holidays; Dezong refused the practice, limiting celebration to ministers' toast for long life.
units.literal: From Suzong onward birthdays became festivals, yet Dezong established no festival—only stopping at ministers raising cups and offering longevity wishes.

units.zh: 代宗繇廣平王復二京，梨園供奉官劉日進制《寶應長寧樂》十八曲以獻，皆宮調也。
units.en: When Daizong, as Prince of Guangping, recovered the two capitals, Pear Garden officer Liu Rijin offered eighteen Precious Response Long Peace pieces, all in palace mode.
units.literal: When Daizong followed Prince of Guangping in recovering the two capitals, Pear Garden tribute officer Liu Rijin composed eighteen pieces of "Precious Response Long Peace Music" to present—all in palace mode.

units.zh: 大曆元年，又有《廣平太一樂》。
units.en: Dali 1 added Guangping Great Unity Music as well.
units.literal: In the first year of Dali there was also "Guangping Great Unity Music."

units.zh: 《涼州曲》，本西涼所獻也，其聲本宮調，有大遍、小遍。
units.en: "Liangzhou Tune," first offered by Western Liang, is rooted in palace mode and exists in long and short versions.
units.literal: "Liangzhou Tune" was originally presented by Western Liang; its sound is fundamentally palace mode, with great and small repetitions.

units.zh: 貞元初，樂工康昆侖寓其聲於琵琶，奏於玉宸殿，因號《玉宸宮調》，合諸樂，則用黃鐘宮。
units.en: In early Zhenyuan Kang Kunlun arranged the tune for pipa and played it in the Jade Hall, naming it Jade Hall Palace Mode; in full ensemble it was set to Huangzhong Palace.
units.literal: Early in Zhenyuan, musician Kang Kunlun set its sound on the pipa and performed it in the Jade Hall Palace; it was therefore called "Jade Hall Palace Mode," and when combined with all music Huangzhong Palace was used.

units.zh: 其後方鎮多制樂舞以獻。
units.en: Later many frontier governors composed dance-music as tribute.
units.literal: Afterward regional commanders often composed music and dance to present.

units.zh: 河東節度使馬燧獻《定難曲》。
units.en: Ma Sui of Hedong offered Settling Hardship.
units.literal: Hedong Military Commissioner Ma Sui presented "Settling Hardship Tune."

units.zh: 昭義軍節度使王虔休以德宗誕辰未有大樂，乃作《繼天誕聖樂》，以宮為調，帝因作《中和樂舞》。
units.en: Wang Qianxiu of Zhaoyi, finding no grand piece for Dezong's birthday, wrote Continuing Heaven Birthday Sage Music in palace mode; the emperor answered with Central Harmony Dance.
units.literal: Zhaoyi Army Military Commissioner Wang Qianxiu, because Dezong's birthday had lacked great music, therefore composed "Continuing Heaven Birthday Sage Music," using palace as mode; the emperor thereupon composed "Central Harmony Music Dance."

units.zh: 山南節度使于頔又獻《順聖樂》，曲將半，而行綴皆伏，一人舞於中，又令女伎為佾舞，雄健壯妙，號《孫武順聖樂》。
units.en: Yu Di of Shannan sent Following Sage Music: midway through, ranks dropped flat while one dancer performed center stage; female performers joined in row dance—fierce and superb—hence Sun Wu Following Sage.
units.literal: Shannan Military Commissioner Yu Di also presented "Following Sage Music"; when the tune was half done the marching ranks all prostrated themselves, one man danced in the center, and he also ordered female performers to perform the row dance—bold, strong, and marvelous—called "Sun Wu Following Sage Music."

units.zh: 文宗好雅樂，詔太常卿馮定采開元雅樂制《雲韶法曲》及《霓裳羽衣舞曲》。
units.en: Wenzong favored court music and had Feng Ding draw on Kaiyuan elegant pieces to create Cloud Suite Fa Tune and Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Robe dance music.
units.literal: Wenzong loved elegant music and ordered Court Director Feng Ding to gather Kaiyuan elegant music and compose "Cloud Suite Fa Tune" and "Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Robe Dance Music."

units.zh: 《雲韶樂》有玉磬四虡，琴、瑟、築、簫、篪、籥、跋膝、笙、竽皆一，登歌四人，分立堂上下，童子五人，繡衣執金蓮花以導，舞者三百人，階下設錦筵，遇內宴乃奏。
units.en: Cloud Suite Music used four tiers of jade chimes plus one each of zither, se, zhu, flute, chi, yue pipe, baxi, sheng, and yu; four ascending vocalists split above and below the hall; five boys in brocade bore golden lotus guides; three hundred dancers on brocade mats below the steps—reserved for palace feasts.
units.literal: "Cloud Suite Music" had four tiers of jade chimes; qin, se, zhu, xiao, chi, yue, baxi, sheng, and yu each one; four ascending singers standing separately above and below the hall; five boys in embroidered robes holding golden lotus flowers as guides; three hundred dancers; brocade mats set below the steps—it was performed only at inner banquets.

units.zh: 謂大臣曰：「笙磬同音，沈吟忘味，不圖為樂至於斯也。」
units.en: He told ministers, "Flute and chime blend as one tone; you linger and forget taste—I never thought music could come to this."
units.literal: He told his ministers: "Sheng and stone chime share one tone; lingering in thought one forgets flavor—I never imagined music could reach this."

units.zh: 自是臣下功高者，輒賜之。
units.en: Thereafter high-merit officials were often granted performances.
units.literal: From then on, whenever a minister's merit was high, it was bestowed on him.

units.zh: 樂成，改法曲為仙韶曲。
units.en: Once finished, the fa tune was retitled Immortal Suite.
units.literal: When the music was completed, the fa tune was renamed the Immortal Suite tune.

units.zh: 會昌初，宰相李德裕命樂工制《萬斯年曲》以獻。
units.en: Early Huichang saw Li Deyu commission Ten Thousand Years for presentation.
units.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, Chancellor Li Deyu ordered musicians to compose "Ten Thousand Years Tune" to present.

units.zh: 大中初，太常樂工五千餘人，俗樂一千五百餘人。
units.en: By early Dazhong the Court of Sacrifices held over five thousand musicians and popular music another fifteen hundred.
units.literal: Early in Dazhong, Court of Sacrifices musicians numbered more than five thousand; popular musicians more than fifteen hundred.

units.zh: 宣宗每宴群臣，備百戲。
units.en: Xuānzong's ministerial banquets always featured the full hundred acts.
units.literal: Xuanzong whenever he feasted ministers provided the hundred entertainments.

units.zh: 帝制新曲，教女伶數十百人，衣珠翠緹繡，連袂而歌，其樂有《播皇猷》曲，舞者高冠方履，褒衣博帶，趨走俯仰，中於規矩。
units.en: He wrote new pieces for dozens of female singers in pearl, jade, and brocade, performing arm in arm; Spreading Imperial Virtue paired high caps and square shoes with flowing robes—every step and bow measured to rule.
units.literal: The emperor composed new tunes and taught several tens or hundreds of female performers, dressed in pearl, kingfisher, and brocade, to sing linked sleeve by sleeve; among the music was the tune "Spreading Imperial Virtue": dancers wore high caps and square shoes, broad robes and wide belts, advancing and bowing within rule.

units.zh: 又有《蔥嶺西曲》，士女蠙歌為隊，其詞言蔥嶺之民樂河，湟故地歸唐也。
units.en: West of Congling had men and women chorus in ranks, lyrics celebrating Congling peoples' joy as He-Huang territories rejoined Tang.
units.literal: There was also "West of Congling Tune": men and women sang in chorus as a troupe; its words say the people of Congling rejoice that the old lands of the He and Huang rivers have returned to Tang.

units.zh: 咸通間，諸王多習音聲、倡優雜戲，天子幸其院，則迎駕奏樂。
units.en: In the Xiantong era princes took up music, singers, and variety acts; when the emperor visited their mansions they greeted him with performance.
units.literal: During Xiantong, many imperial princes studied sound, music, singers, actors, and mixed plays; when the Son of Heaven visited their halls they welcomed the carriage with music.

units.zh: 是時，蕃鎮稍復舞《破陣樂》，然舞者衣畫甲，執旗旆，才十人而已。
units.en: Frontier commands then revived Breaking the Formation, but only about ten dancers in painted armor carrying flags.
units.literal: At that time frontier commands somewhat revived dancing "Breaking the Formation Music," yet the dancers wore painted armor and held banners and flags—only about ten people.

units.zh: 蓋唐之盛時，樂曲所傳，至其末年，往往亡缺。
units.en: Tunes handed down from Tang's height were largely broken or lost by dynasty's end.
units.literal: Generally the pieces transmitted from Tang's flourishing age, reaching its final years, were often lost and incomplete.

units.zh: 周、隋與北齊、陳接壤，故歌舞雜有四方之樂。
units.en: Zhou and Sui lay against Northern Qi and Chen, so dance and song mixed music from every quarter.
units.literal: Zhou and Sui bordered Northern Qi and Chen; thus song and dance mixed music from all four directions.

units.zh: 至唐，東夷樂有高麗、百濟，北狄有鮮卑、吐谷渾、部落稽，南蠻有扶南、天竺、南詔、驃國，西戎有高昌、龜茲、疏勒、康國、安國，凡十四國之樂，而八國之伎，列于十部樂。
units.en: Under Tang, Eastern Yi included Koguryo and Baekje; Northern Di, Xianbei, Tuyuhun, and Buluoji; Southern Man, Funan, Tianzhu, Nanzhao, and Pyu; Western Rong, Gaochang, Kucha, Shule, Kang, and An—fourteen traditions, eight of which entered the Ten Sections repertoire.
units.literal: Reaching Tang: Eastern Yi music had Koguryo and Baekje; Northern Di had Xianbei, Tuyuhun, and Buluoji; Southern Man had Funan, Tianzhu, Nanzhao, and Pyu; Western Rong had Gaochang, Kucha, Shule, Kang, and An—fourteen states' music in all, while eight states' performances were listed in the Ten Sections Music.

units.zh: 中宗時，百濟樂工人亡散，岐王為太常卿，復奏置之，然音伎多闕。
units.en: Under Zhongzong Baekje players dispersed; Prince of Qi, as Court Director, restored the troupe, but much technique was gone.
units.literal: In Zhongzong's time Baekje musicians scattered and were lost; Prince of Qi as Court Director memorialized to restore and install them, yet most musical skills were missing.

units.zh: 舞者二人，紫大袖裙襦、章甫冠、衣履。
units.en: Two dancers wore purple wide-sleeved jackets and skirts with zhangfu caps and full dress.
units.literal: Two dancers wore purple great-sleeved jackets and skirts, zhangfu caps, and robes and shoes.

units.zh: 樂有箏、笛、桃皮觱篥、箜篌、歌而已。
units.en: Instrumentation was limited to zheng, flute, peach-bark bili, konghou, and voice.
units.literal: The music had only zheng, di, peach-bark bili, konghou, and song.

units.zh: 北狄樂皆馬上之聲，自漢後以為鼓吹，亦軍中樂，馬上奏之，故隸鼓吹署。
units.en: Northern Di pieces are cavalry music; since Han they served as drum-and-pipe and field music played mounted, hence their place under the Drum-and-Pipe Office.
units.literal: Northern Di music is all sound on horseback; from Han onward it was taken as drum-and-pipe, also military music, performed on horseback; therefore it is attached to the Drum-and-Pipe Office.

units.zh: 後魏樂府初有《北歌》，亦曰《真人歌》，都代時，命宮人朝夕歌之。
units.en: Northern Wei's bureau first kept Northern Song, also True Man Song, sung morning and evening by palace women at the Dai capital.
units.literal: Northern Wei Music Bureau at first had "Northern Song," also called "True Man Song"; in the capital of Dai, palace women were ordered to sing it morning and evening.

units.zh: 周、隋始與西涼樂雜奏。
units.en: Zhou and Sui began interleaving it with Western Liang pieces.
units.literal: Zhou and Sui only then mixed it with Western Liang music in performance.

units.zh: 至唐存者五十三章，而名可解者六章而已：一曰《慕容可汗》，二曰《吐谷渾》，三曰《部落稽》，四曰《钜鹿公主》，五曰《白淨王》，六曰《太子企喻》也。
units.en: Tang preserved fifty-three sections but only six titles are intelligible: Murong Khan, Tuyuhun, Buluoji, Princess of Julu, King Pure White, and Crown Prince Qiyu.
units.literal: By Tang fifty-three chapters survived, yet only six titles can be understood: first "Murong Khan," second "Tuyuhun," third "Buluoji," fourth "Princess of Julu," fifth "King Pure White," sixth "Crown Prince Qiyu."

units.zh: 其餘辭多可汗之稱，蓋燕、魏之際鮮卑歌也。
units.en: Other lyrics mostly address khans—Xianbei songs from the Yan–Wei period.
units.literal: The rest of the texts mostly use the title khan—basically Xianbei songs from the Yan and Wei era.

units.zh: 隋鼓吹有其曲而不同。
units.en: Sui drum-and-pipe kept related pieces in altered form.
units.literal: Sui drum-and-pipe had the same pieces but differently.

units.zh: 貞觀中，將軍侯貴昌，并州人，世傳《北歌》，詔隸太樂，然譯者不能通，歲久不可辨矣。
units.en: Zhenguan general Hou Guichang of Bingzhou, hereditary keeper of Northern Song, entered Grand Music by edict, but translators could not parse it and the text faded beyond recognition.
units.literal: In Zhenguan, General Hou Guichang, a Bingzhou man, transmitted "Northern Song" for generations; an edict attached him to Grand Music, yet translators could not understand it; over the years it became indistinguishable.

units.zh: 金吾所掌有大角，即魏之「簸邏回」，工人謂之角手，以備鼓吹。
units.en: The Golden Crow office held the great horn—Wei's "boluo hui"—whose players, called horn hands, backed the drum-and-pipe ensemble.
units.literal: What the Golden Crow guard controls is the great horn—namely Wei's "boluo hui"; craftsmen call them horn players, to supply drum-and-pipe.

units.zh: 南蠻、北狄俗斷髮，故舞者以繩圍首約髮。
units.en: Southern Man and Northern Di wore cropped hair, so dancers bound their heads with cord.
units.literal: Southern Man and Northern Di customarily cut their hair short; therefore dancers bound the head with cord to secure the hair.

units.zh: 有新聲自河西至者，號胡音，龜茲散樂皆為之少息。
units.en: Fresh melodies from the Hexi corridor were labeled barbarian tones, briefly eclipsing even Kucha repertoire.
units.literal: When new sounds arrived from west of the river they were called barbarian tones, and Kucha scattered music all quieted somewhat for them.

units.zh: 扶南樂，舞者二人，以朝霞為衣，赤皮鞋。
units.en: Funan used two dancers in dawn-colored robes and red leather shoes.
units.literal: Funan music: two dancers wore dawn-glow colored robes and red leather shoes.

units.zh: 天竺伎能自斷手足，刺腸胃，高宗惡其驚俗，詔不令入中國。
units.en: Tianzhu acts mutilated limbs and pierced bellies; Gaozong banned them as offensive to custom.
units.literal: Tianzhu performers could sever their own hands and feet and pierce their bowels; Gaozong detested their shock to custom and ordered them not admitted into China.

units.zh: 睿宗時，婆羅門國獻人倒行以足舞，仰植銛刀，俯身就鋒，曆臉下，復植於背，觱篥者立腹上，終曲而不傷。
units.en: Ruizong received a Brahman who danced upside down on his feet, bowed to upright blades along his face, replanted them on his back, and bore a bili player on his belly unharmed through the finale.
units.literal: In Ruizong's time Brahman kingdom presented a man who danced walking on his feet inverted; planting sharp knives upright, he bent his body toward the blades, passed down his face, and planted them again on his back; a bili player stood on his belly—through the whole piece he was unharmed.

units.zh: 又伏伸其手，二人躡之，周旋百轉。
units.en: He would stretch prone with hands extended while two men stepped on them and spun a hundred circuits.
units.literal: He also lay prostrate extending his hands; two men trod on them and wheeled a hundred turns.

units.zh: 開元初，其樂猶與四夷樂同列。
units.en: Early Kaiyuan it still shared billing with the four foreign ensembles.
units.literal: Early Kaiyuan its music still ranked with the four barbarian musics.

units.zh: 貞元中，南詔異牟尋遺使詣劍南西川節度使韋皋，言欲獻夷中歌曲，且令驃國進樂。
units.en: Zhenyuan saw Nanzhao's Yi Mouxun ask Wei Gao, southwest commissioner, to receive barbarian songs and send Pyu musicians as well.
units.literal: In Zhenyuan, Nanzhao's Yi Mouxun sent envoys to Southwest Military Commissioner Wei Gao, saying he wished to present songs from among the barbarians and also ordered Pyu to advance music.

units.zh: 皋乃作《南詔奉聖樂》，用黃鐘之均，舞六成，工六十四人，贊引二人，序曲二十八疊，執羽而舞「南詔奉聖樂」字，曲將終，雷鼓作於四隅，舞者皆拜，金聲作而起，執羽稽首，以象朝覲。
units.en: Gao wrote Nanzhao Offering Sage Music in the Huangzhong register—six dance sections, sixty-four players, two announcers, twenty-eight prelude repetitions. Dancers bore feathers spelling "Nanzhao Offering Sage Music"; at the close thunder drums at four corners sent them prostrate, then metal tones raised them to bow with feathers in mimicry of imperial audience.
units.literal: Gao then composed "Nanzhao Offering Sage Music," using the Huangzhong register; six dance sections, sixty-four craftsmen, two presenters; introductory music twenty-eight repetitions; holding feathers they danced the words "Nanzhao Offering Sage Music"; as the tune neared its end thunder drums sounded at the four corners and all dancers bowed; when metal sound rose they stood, holding feathers and bowing forehead to ground, to represent court audience.

units.zh: 每拜跪，節以鉦鼓。
units.en: Every bow and kneel was timed to cymbals and drums.
units.literal: Each bow and kneel was paced by cymbal and drum.

units.zh: 又為五均：一曰黃鐘，宮之宮；
units.en: He also set five registers: Huangzhong as palace-of-palace;
units.literal: He also made five registers: first, Huangzhong, palace of palace;

units.zh: 二曰太蔟，商之宮；
units.en: Taicu as palace-of-shang;
units.literal: second, Taicu, palace of shang;

units.zh: 三曰姑洗，角之宮；
units.en: Guxian as palace-of-jiao;
units.literal: third, Guxian, palace of jiao;

units.zh: 四曰林鐘，徵之宮；
units.en: Linzhong as palace-of-zhi;
units.literal: fourth, Linzhong, palace of zhi;

units.zh: 五曰南呂，羽之宮。
units.en: Nanlü as palace-of-yu.
units.literal: fifth, Nanlü, palace of yu.

units.zh: 其文義繁雜，不足復紀。
units.en: The textual glosses are too tangled to record in full.
units.literal: Its text and meaning are tangled and complex—not worth recording further.

units.zh: 德宗閱於麟德殿，以授太常工人，自是殿庭宴則立奏，宮中則坐奏。
units.en: Dezong reviewed it at Linde Hall and passed it to court craftsmen; thereafter hall feasts used standing performance, palace feasts seated.
units.literal: Dezong reviewed it at Linde Hall and handed it to Court of Sacrifices craftsmen; from then on at hall banquets it was performed standing, within the palace seated.

units.zh: 十七年，驃國王雍羌遣弟悉利移、城主舒難陀獻其國樂，至成都，韋皋復譜次其聲，又圖其舞容、樂器以獻。
units.en: Year 17 brought Pyu King Yongyao's brother Xilayi and lord Shunantuo with state music to Chengdu; Wei Gao re-harmonized it and submitted illustrations of dances and instruments.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year Pyu King Yongyao sent his younger brother Xilayi and fortress lord Shunantuo to present their state's music; reaching Chengdu, Wei Gao again arranged its sounds and also drew its dance forms and instruments to present.

units.zh: 凡工器二十有二，其音八：金、貝、絲、竹、匏、革、牙、角，大抵皆夷狄之器，其聲曲不隸於有司，故無足采雲。
units.en: Twenty-two instruments covered eight tones—metal, shell, silk, bamboo, gourd, hide, ivory, horn—mostly foreign. Because their repertoire lay outside regular bureaus, the account ends here.
units.literal: Instruments in all numbered twenty-two; their sounds eight: metal, shell, silk, bamboo, gourd, hide, ivory, and horn—mostly all barbarian instruments; their pieces and tunes are not under any bureau's jurisdiction, therefore not worth recording in detail.
